items.headline: FDA approves first drug in a new class to prevent repeat strokes
items.summary: The FDA approved asundexian, a once-daily pill that blocks a clotting protein called Factor Eleven-A, to help prevent a second stroke in adults who already had a mild to moderate one. In a trial of more than twelve thousand patients, it cut the risk of another stroke by about a quarter without raising the overall rate of serious bleeding.
items.why_it_matters: It's the first approved medicine in an entirely new class of blood thinners, giving stroke survivors a safer option for preventing a second, often more disabling stroke.

items.headline: FDA approves new pill for a painful joint tumor with few treatment options
items.summary: The FDA approved pimicotinib, a once-daily pill for adults with symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumor, a rare tumor that grows inside joints and can cause pain and reduced mobility. In a placebo-controlled trial, more than half of patients taking the drug saw their tumors shrink, compared to only a few taking placebo.
items.why_it_matters: It gives patients with this painful, often hard to treat joint tumor an effective new daily pill, adding to a short list of approved options.
